done.why: I had seen a good slice and had no clear goal; stopped after collecting items in the gazebo.

about: A Zork-style cave adventure: a barrow, a cavern with a ravine, a wizard who has hoarded the Empire's treasures south of the ravine, and a garden with a gazebo.

ending.what: None reached; I only began to explore.

moments.note: The Wizard appeared, spoke at me, and made me drop the lamp.
Going south into the dark said a grue might eat me; I did not know to light the lamp until I tried it.
The gazebo with a tea table of items and a newspaper that explained the story.

wished: A clearer sense of what my goal was.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you
lines.why: It gave me a goal in a natural way.

lines.line: the public is advised not to let him finish a word.
lines.why: It was funny and explained the Wizard.

fun.why: Pleasant to wander, with a few surprises, but I stopped early.

engagement.why: The goal hint pulled me on, but nothing urgent held me.

difficulty.why: Plain commands worked and there was no real obstacle in the part I saw.

interestingness.why: The Wizard's wordless reaction to my empty hands felt reactive and clever.

prose.why: Clear, atmospheric room descriptions with some wit.
